ranked_hypotheses.name: Deconfounded Two-Host En-Echelon Relay-Ramp & Geodetic-Geophysical Stepover Transfer Corridor
layers: data/bridge/existing_faults.tif (visible fold subset only in holdout; 60,988 full-catalogue pixels)

ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: In Walker Lane and Great Basin extensional/transtensional systems (Peacock & Sanderson 1994; Faulds & Varga 1998; Curewitz & Karson 1997; Faulds et al. 2006), displacement between two stepping-over fault segments C1 != C2 is transferred across a tilted relay ramp bounded by synthetic/antithetic breaching cross-faults and tip splays. Using vendor/gems57/relay_bend_anatomy.py (two_host_frame exact bitplane second-host EDT and host_bend_fields spin-2 multi-scale turning) coupled with geodetic transtensional strain (geod_shearrate x |geod_dilaterate|) and across-ramp basement-depth/gravity transfer gradients (|grad(depth_to_base_surf)| x iso_grav_anom_hg), and deconfounded on training positives via 5-bucket Buffered-Component Leave-Bucket-Out (B-LBCO) to eliminate the d1=0 self-collapse tautology (IR-H84-01).
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Coalescing alluvial-fan interfluve sutures (bajada saddles between adjacent range-front canyons) and buried paleochannel or volcanic dike bridges between neighboring bedrock spurs can produce intermediate gravity/magnetic gradients inside a morphological gap between two mapped fault segments without brittle relay breaching.
ranked_hypotheses.how_it_differs_from_repo: First lane in GEMSDOE77 to execute vendor/gems57/relay_bend_anatomy.py (two_host_frame bitplane two-host geometry and host_bend_fields spin-2 multi-scale turning) and solve the Relay-Stepover Self-Collapse Tautology (IR-H84-01) via 5-bucket B-LBCO deconfounding coupled with geodetic strain and basement-step transfer.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Upward-Continuation Vertical Derivative Ratio (Depth-Selective Magnetic/Gravity Spectral Decay Index)
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Ratio of vertical gradient to upward-continued horizontal gradient (TMI_VG / |grad U_dz(RTP)|) isolating shallow-to-intermediate brittle fault offsets (0.2-1.5 km depth) from deep plutonic roots (>4 km) and superficial float noise (<50 m).
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Shallow basaltic lava flow margins and terraced pediment gravel caps.
ranked_hypotheses.how_it_differs_from_repo: H77G used raw TMI demagnetization troughs; H84-2 uses the spectral depth-decay ratio between vertical gradient and upward-continued RTP.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Seismic b-Value & Depth-Stratified Microseismic Swarm Asymmetry Projected Up Dip-Slip Hanging Walls
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Cross-strike offset between earthquake density (deq_n100a15) and potency/intensity (ieq_n100a15) projected up a 60-degree normal-fault dip plane from brittle-ductile basement depth to the surface trace.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Geothermal injection/production induced seismicity clusters and volcanic caldera swarm clouds.
ranked_hypotheses.how_it_differs_from_repo: H77-TSD used isotropic scalar difference z(deq) - z(ieq); H84-3 projects seismic swarm asymmetry up the hanging-wall dip vector to the surface trace.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Radiometric Uranium-to-Thorium Redox Mobilization Front (U/Th x MT Conductance Gradient)
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Hexavalent uranium (U6+) is soluble in oxidizing meteoric/geothermal fluids while thorium (Th4+) is immobile in resistate phases; redox fronts along active fluid-conducting faults create sharp cross-strike U/Th step anomalies paired with smectite clay-cap conductance margins (|grad cond_surf|).
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Evaporitic playa uranium concentration and felsic ash-flow tuff outcrops.
ranked_hypotheses.how_it_differs_from_repo: H79-RH used K/Th illitization halos and H82-TCSTEP used total-count radiometrics; H84-4 targets redox-sensitive U/Th fractionation across MT conductance boundaries.

ranked_hypotheses.name: Geomorphic Piedmont Fan-Head Trenching & Drainage-Spacing Spectral Periodicity Deficit
ranked_hypotheses.physical_signature: Active range-front and piedmont normal faults disrupt regular Wallace (1978) / Hovius (1996) along-strike canyon-spacing periodicity and cause fan-head incision waves measurable via local 1-D wavelet variance along range-front contours.
ranked_hypotheses.named_non_fault_mimic: Lithologic sill resistance steps and Pleistocene pluvial lake highstand wave-cut notches.
ranked_hypotheses.how_it_differs_from_repo: H77E-Knick used stream chi and k_sn knickpoints; H84-5 measures along-strike drainage spacing regularity breakdown on alluvial fans.
